name: Pi-hole
description: Block ads and trackers for every device in your home, including phones and TVs.

afterInstall.text: Click Open and log in with the Admin password shown on this page.
Tell your devices to use Pi-hole, following the steps under "On your devices" below. Changing the router covers every device at once.
Check that it works: on the Pi-hole dashboard, Total queries starts growing as your devices browse.

default.text: Pi-hole needs port 53, the standard port for DNS. Most Linux systems leave it free, so there is usually nothing to do.
If the install says port 53 is already used, open a terminal on the server and see which program holds it:
Stop or reconfigure that program, then install Pi-hole again.

windows.text: With Docker Desktop there is usually nothing to do on the server.
If the install says port 53 is already used, the Windows feature Internet Connection Sharing may hold it. Open the Start menu, type Services and open it.
Find Internet Connection Sharing (ICS), open it, click Stop and set Startup type to Disabled. Then install Pi-hole again.
If Windows asks whether Docker Desktop may accept connections, allow it on private networks.

macos.text: With Docker Desktop there is usually nothing to do on the server.
If macOS asks whether Docker may accept incoming connections, click Allow.
If the install says port 53 is already used, another DNS app is running on this Mac (for example a VPN or dnsmasq). Quit it and install Pi-hole again.

router.text: Open your router's settings page in a browser. The address is usually printed on a label on the router, often http://192.168.1.1 or http://192.168.0.1.
Find the DNS server setting for your home network. It is usually under LAN or DHCP settings, not under Internet or WAN.
Set the primary DNS server to {serverAddress}. Leave the secondary DNS empty, otherwise devices may skip Pi-hole.
Save, then turn Wi-Fi off and on again on your devices so they pick up the change.

windows.text: Open Settings, then Network & internet, then Wi-Fi (or Ethernet), and click your network.
Next to DNS server assignment click Edit, choose Manual and turn on IPv4.
Set Preferred DNS to {serverAddress} and click Save.

macos.text: Open System Settings, then Network, and select your Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection.
Click Details, then DNS. Click + and enter {serverAddress}.
Remove any other DNS servers in the list, then click OK.

linux.text: Open Settings, then Wi-Fi or Network, and click the gear next to your connection.
Open the IPv4 tab, turn off Automatic next to DNS and enter {serverAddress}.
Click Apply, then disconnect and reconnect. Other desktops have the same option in their network settings.

android.text: Android only lets you change DNS per Wi-Fi network together with a fixed IP address, which is fiddly. Changing the router instead is much easier.
If you still want to: open Settings, then Network & internet, then Internet, and tap the gear next to your Wi-Fi.
Tap Edit, open Advanced options, set IP settings to Static and enter {serverAddress} as DNS 1. Keep the IP address and gateway it suggests, then Save.

ios.text: Open Settings, then Wi-Fi, and tap the (i) next to your network.
Tap Configure DNS, choose Manual and delete the existing servers.
Tap Add Server, enter {serverAddress} and tap Save.
